newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end firmer, gold bounces back.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end firmer, gold bounces back.

text.p: New York precious metals ended firmer as jittery financial markets and further gains in silver helped gold make healthy gains, traders said.
Gold initially benefitted from a mid-morning fund-led boost in silver, to encourage the yellow metal to catch up with silver after the latter's gains last week, traders said.
"There is a very jittery tone in general in the financial markets which is benefitting the precious metals," said William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch.
So called ratio trading, or buying silver and selling gold, had also probably run its course, O'Neill added.
March COMEX silver settled at its highest level since $5.058 on Oct 23.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was near the day's low of 6635.68 points when COMEX gold closed, some 60 points down on the day, but later recovered slightly.
COMEX February gold went out $3.90 higher at $357.30 an ounce, traded $357.80 to $353.20. It was February's highest close in two weeks.
Bullion was quoted by dealers at $356.00/50.
March COMEX silver settled 7.0 cents higher at $5.047, traded $5.055 to $4.94. Traders said the market was making an attempt to test $5.06 in March but ran into resistance and selling around $5.05.
Volumes in gold and silver trading were estimated at 50,000 lots and 22,000 lots, respectively.
Clutching gold and silver's coattails, the white metals ended firmer, with April NYMEX platinum $1.70 higher at $364.30 and March NYMEX palladium $0.25 firmer at $125.80.
COMEX silver stocks on Monday rose 279,170 ounces to 194,813,066 ounces, while gold stocks increased 47,475 ounces to 737,041 ounces.
Existing homes sales in December fell sharply, partly due to cold weather during the month, the National Association of Realtors said.

Sales fell 3.5 percent in December to a annual rate of 3.87 million from a revised rate of 4.01 million in November, NAR said. Wall Street economist had forecast a sales rate of 4.0 million in December.
